equivalent: Two guards, one invariant. This is the PRE-check on the unlocked snapshot; `_guards` re-checks the fresh row under the lock and refuses there. Probed 2026-08-16: removing either one alone leaves test_provisional_row_never_reaches_long green, removing BOTH fails it, so the invariant is covered and each copy is defense in depth. The job only the IN-LOCK copy can do — catching a row that changed after the snapshot — is now pinned by test_a_row_contested_between_the_snapshot_and_the_lock_is_refused. What only the pre-check does is short-circuit before taking the lock and log a distinct line: cost and legibility, not correctness.
